DEV_FIELD_CONFIG_SLIDE.BEST_PRACTICES_CONTENT:
Use PloomesServer to make requests:

● PloomesServer is a class designed to make it possible to make requests to the ploomes API or other APIs from the developer field.

● Here is the link to the documentation for the PloomesServer class (portuguese): https://www.notion.so/Ploomes-Server-a77a4a551b284f3eae3bbefadb823565

● Here is the link to the Ploomes API documentation (portuguese): https://developers.ploomes.com/

Use PloomesDocument to manipulate the HTML outside the iframe:

● Because the developer field is rendered in an iframe, it does not have access to the HTML that is outside the field, if you need to access it you can use the PloomesDocument object which is the HTML document that is outside the iframe.

● The PloomesDocument object does not work on mobile, because mobile contains different code than web and does not have a document object.

● Here is a link to the documentation for the document object: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Document

Do not inject code into existing Ploomes html:

● This kind of practice creates inconsistent and insecure code, because Ploomes can update and the identifier used to inject the code can disappear on an update, thus making the field code no longer work.

● If you need this kind of behavior, we recommend that you create a modal or a floating component.

Do not use setInterval:

● The code entered in setInterval will continue to execute even after the user leaves the screen where the field is rendered, so inserting a setInterval is inserting code that will remain in processing and memory competition with Ploomes until the user hits F5.

● When inside a trigger, a new setInterval will be created each time the formula is called, thus generating very heavy and costly code.

Be careful about the performance of your code:

● Remember that the processing of your code competes with the processing of Ploomes, so heavy code can slow Ploomes down, so use common sense.

Do not put access keys in the code:

● Remember that the code you configure for this field can be easily accessed by users using the browser's element inspector. Therefore, by adding an access key in the configuration (userKey from Ploomes integration user, for example), it can be easily collected and used by an ordinary user.

● For operations of this type, use the PloomesServer class. This class was developed specifically for these cases, and from it you can collect the userKey securely, as well as making it easier to use the Ploomes API.
